executionPolicy: Sequential workflow execution; activities within each workflow run with bounded native parallelism. Local isolated trial runs precede native daemon runs.

workflows.conference: XIX Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2025), co-located with SBBD
workflows.scope: Four complete labeled NAB artificialWithAnomaly source series curated by UniTED, with no point subsampling. ARIMA(2,0,2) and a causal rolling-residual baseline are Python adapters; they are not the original R/Harbinger implementation and do not claim paper-metric equivalence. Detectors fit thresholds on the first 25% and are scored on the remaining observations with point-wise labels; no temporal-tolerance NAB score is claimed. These artificial signals are original benchmark inputs, not locally generated substitutes. Original upstream benchmark: https://github.com/numenta/NAB. UniTED code: MIT; upstream dataset conditions remain applicable.

workflows.conference: XX Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2026), co-located with SBBD
workflows.scope: Re-execute the original UCS, Greedy and A* notebook functions over the complete frozen curated graph: 108 nodes, 226 directed edges, all 11,556 distinct ordered origin–destination pairs for each of three original cost profiles. Nine independent search activities produce 104,004 searches. This reproduces the search stage, not the upstream geographic source reconstruction. The paper reports 3,715 Greedy divergences; the workflow measures and reports actual agreement. Original data deposit: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20867698. Deposit metadata states CC BY 4.0; its README contains provisional code-license wording, so no broader code redistribution license is inferred.

workflows.conference: XVIII Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2024), co-located with SBBD
workflows.scope: Execute the original PL/pgSQL functions and both original 2D/3D CUBE queries on all 569 original Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer observations supplied by the authors. Each query gets an isolated PostgreSQL/PostGIS instance, so parallel activities do not mutate one another’s clustering state. Transport path is adapted and PostgreSQL random seed is fixed to 0.42 for the authors’ generated hospital/date dimensions. Hospital locations and dates are illustrative generated dimensions, not clinical provenance. Runtime uses PostgreSQL 15/PostGIS 3 on Debian Bookworm rather than the paper’s PostgreSQL 16.3; result semantics, not timing equivalence, are checked. Original dataset: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/17/breast+cancer+wisconsin+diagnostic . Upstream repository has no explicit code license; no redistribution grant is inferred.

workflows.conference: XX Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2026), co-located with SBBD
workflows.scope: Run the original R ETLs for the complete climate, bioenergy and emissions source tables, followed by the original miniature-generation script. Each newly generated complete R object is compared semantically with the authors’ published full object at the same commit; published objects are references only, never substituted for ETL output. This is a three-collection instantiation of Eidolon, not every collection or remote publication. Origin: FAOSTAT https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/ET , https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/BE and https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/GT . Code is MIT; source data retain FAO terms. Three independent ETL branches and three dependent miniaturization activities expose real parallelism.

workflows.conference: XIX Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2025), co-located with SBBD
workflows.scope: Process all original hourly CSVs for São Paulo–Mirante station A701 from 2013 through 2022, the station and period illustrated by the paper. Execute the original notebook ingestion/normalization and cleaning definitions (cells 16 and 20), then generate noninteractive temperature, precipitation and humidity analyses. Yearly ingestion activities are independent; the original cleaning runs once after concatenation, preserving cross-year filling. Raw inputs come from the nested dataset.zip in the original Zenodo deposit, acquired by verified ZIP members through HTTP byte ranges. The entire 1.92 GB parent archive is not downloaded or claimed to have a newly verified global hash; extracted member CRC and SHA-256 are checked. Original notebook and data: CC BY 4.0. INMET source portal: https://portal.inmet.gov.br/dadoshistoricos . No processed author outputs are used as computation inputs.

workflows.conference: XX Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2026), co-located with SBBD
authors: Cândido Alfredo Carvalho de Lucena Filho
workflows.scope: Portable reproduction profile: five complete original UFRJ recordings from each of six fault classes (30 recordings, selected deterministically across each archive). Execute the original notebook’s 132-feature extraction and neural architecture definitions; retain its 2,048-sample window, 1,024 hop and maximum 50 windows per recording. Run five-fold group-aware evaluation with complete relative recording paths as group IDs. Default training is shortened to 10 epochs (LSTM 5); AKOFLOW_PROFILE=standard uses 50 (LSTM 15). Quantization uses the final fold model, calibrates only on its training recordings and evaluates only on held-out recordings. These explicit protocol adaptations avoid mixing training observations into quantization evaluation; results do not claim to reproduce the paper’s F1=0.98 or on-device memory/latency. No physical microcontroller is tested. Original data creators: Signals, Multimedia and Telecommunications Laboratory, COPPE/Poli/UFRJ; source https://www02.smt.ufrj.br/~offshore/mfs/page_01.html . The original notebook and data remain attributed to their authors; no license is inferred from public availability.

workflows.conference: XVIII Brazilian e-Science Workshop (BreSci 2024), co-located with SBBD
workflows.scope: Portable audit of Q1 from the published repository, using genuine TPC-H dbgen 2.13.0 at scale factor 0.01 (complete generated lineitem table). The original MongoDB pipeline filters through 1998-12-01 while the original PostgreSQL query filters through 1998-09-02. Run both unchanged, then an explicitly named aligned variant that changes only MongoDB’s cutoff to 1998-09-02. Execute each engine/mode with and without an index in isolated database instances. Validate numerical equivalence only for aligned semantics and record original-source disagreement. This is a Q1 audit, not reproduction of all 22 queries, the paper’s hardware, scale or performance ranking. Timings under concurrent execution are observations, not a controlled database benchmark. Original data generator and specification: https://www.tpc.org/tpch/ and https://github.com/electrum/tpch-dbgen/tree/32f1c1b92d1664dba542e927d23d86ffa57aa253. TPC-H data are generated by definition; no hand-built fixture replaces them. Original code authors retain attribution; upstream has no explicit license declaration. MongoDB binary is obtained from its official distribution; respective upstream terms apply.
